title: How to Make AI UGC Ads Look and Sound Real, Not Fake or Robotic
summary: Make AI UGC ads look and sound real: a plain script, a matched voice, phone-style vertical framing, one acting cue per line and a take-by-take review checklist.
body_markdown:
## How do you fix stiff, robotic movement?


Stiffness usually starts with over-direction. Asking for a smile, a head tilt, a hand gesture and a raised eyebrow in one line exaggerates the face. Use one acting direction per line and describe the feeling in loose, natural words rather than exact movements.


Then review each take frame by frame. Check hands and fingers, lettering on packaging and screens, product shape and color, lip sync and eye focus. Common AI video failures include a product that does not match the real item, garbled lettering and a hand with the wrong number of fingers. Meta's[Ad Creative Generative AI Terms](https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/ad_creative_generative_ai_terms) make the advertiser solely responsible for checking the accuracy of output from Meta's own tools, and we apply the same discipline to any vendor.


Watch each take twice, once with sound and once muted. The muted pass shows whether captions carry the claim, and the sound pass shows whether the voice fits the face. Fix the failure you find before you regenerate, because a new take can introduce a new problem.


## When is a real creator the better choice?


Some ads need a real person's account. Meta's[partnership ads documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/ad-creative/partnership-ads) describes ads run from a creator's or other partner's handle, which an AI presenter does not have. Use a real customer or creator when your claim depends on someone's own experience, and get permission and clear disclosure.


As of October 2026, creator platforms such as[Billo](https://billo.app/) list partnership ads from creator handles among their services. For a cost comparison of the two routes, see[AI UGC vs creator UGC cost](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-ugc-vs-creator-ugc-cost) .

## Key takeaways


- Fix the script first: plain, problem-led lines with one provable claim and no fake customer voice.
- Export 9:16 and 4:5 with captions, and keep the presenter inside the safe zone.
- Match the voice to the presenter's apparent age, gender and accent, then match the room.
- Give one acting direction per line, and review hands, lettering, product and lip sync frame by frame.
- Use a real creator when the ad must run from a person's handle or rely on their experience.


## FAQ


### How do I make AI UGC voices sound natural?


Match the voice to the presenter's apparent age, gender and accent, and write lines as spoken phrases with natural pauses. Add light room tone so the audio fits a handheld recording. Listen on phone speakers before approving, because a voice that is too clean for the picture will stand out there.


### How do I make AI UGC look like it was filmed on a phone?


Use a vertical frame, handheld-style movement, natural light and a plain background. Keep captions on screen, since Reels play with sound on unless viewers turn it off and some viewers scroll muted anyway. Avoid cinematic grading and studio-style lighting.


### Why do my AI UGC ads look stiff and robotic?


The direction is usually too heavy: several acting cues in one line, too many gestures, or a script that reads like marketing copy. Cut to one cue per line, describe the feeling in loose words rather than exact movements, and rewrite any line you would not say to a friend.


### How do I make AI UGC that looks realistic?


Choose a natural still, use a believable script and a phone-style edit, then review each take against the checklist of hands, lettering, product accuracy and lip sync. Realism depends on all of these together, so fix the weakest element first rather than switching tools.
